info.bio:
Pantera fue formada en Arlington, Texas, en 1981, por los guitarristas Darrell Abbott (apodado "Diamond Darrell" o "Dimebag Darrell") y Terry "Terrence Lee" Glaze, el bajista Tommy Bradford y el baterista Vinnie Paul, hermano de Darrell. Empezaron tocando covers de Kiss y Van Halen, así como material propio encuadrado dentro del glam metal y el hair metal, en clubes nocturnos de Texas.

Pantera lanzó tres olvidados álbumes (Metal Magic, Projects In The Jungle y I Am The Night), antes de descartar al cantante Terry Glaze.

scenes.name: Metal agresivo: Pantera y el metalcore
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Las excepciones a la muerte del metal no son lite metal: cambian el poder del heavy por la agresión. Pantera debuta en una multinacional con Cowboys from Hell (1990), que ni entra en los 200; sin radio y con poca presencia en Headbangers Ball, a base de giras, Far Beyond Driven llega al número uno en 1994. Ese año Slayer coloca Divine Intervention en el top ten. Del cruce entre thrash y hardcore sale el llamado metalcore, con voces entrecortadas y poca melodía: Pantera, Biohazard y Machine Head.

scenes.name: La bestia ha vuelto: OzzFest y las reuniones
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A finales de siglo el metal vuelve a la corriente principal. Con el alternativo moribundo y la electrónica sin despegar, el público fiel sigue ahí: tres mil personas esperan cinco horas en un centro comercial de Chicago en 1998 a que Black Sabbath les firme discos. El detonante es el OzzFest de 1997, organizado por la mánager de Ozzy, que vende más que Lollapalooza con Pantera, Machine Head, Fear Factory, Type O Negative, Neurosis, tres cuartas partes de Black Sabbath y Marilyn Manson, cuyas provocaciones atraen protestas cristianas y titulares. Metallica vuelve a tocar su thrash en directo y en Garage Inc.; Judas Priest ficha a Tim «Ripper» Owens, cantante de una banda tributo llamada British Steel; Mötley Crüe recupera a Vince Neil, Kiss se reúne en 1998, Dickinson regresa a Iron Maiden y Black Sabbath hace en 1999 una gira de reunión con disco de oro. Weinstein ve en ese regreso el gusto «prole» de la cultura de fin de siglo, un contrapeso a la feminización del pop y la ansiedad milenarista: la bestia se niega a morir.

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Phil Anselmo's 1996 Overdose
podcast.body: On July 13, 1996, Pantera frontman Phil Anselmo suffered a heroin overdose, leading to cardiac arrest. His heart stopped for four minutes. "Phil and Selmo of Pantera OD'd on heroin on July 13th, 1996. Cardiac arrest for four minutes."

podcast.title: Pantera Damaged the Stanley Cup at a 1999 Dallas Stars Party
podcast.body: The metal band Pantera caused damage to the Stanley Cup during a party with the Dallas Stars hockey team in 1999, reportedly throwing it into a swimming pool. The incident was covered up with a fabricated story about the trophy being accidentally dropped getting off a plane. "Caused damage to the Stanley Cup during a party with the Dallas Stars, throwing it into a swimming pool."

xref.title: Death in Car Crash (1984)
xref.body: In 1984, drummer Razzle died in a car crash while being driven by Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil. Neil, who was drunk and speeding in his 1972 Ford Pantera, lost control and collided with two other cars, with Razzle dying at the hospital. "Razzle died in hospital."

xref.title: Vehicular Manslaughter of Razzle (1984)
xref.body: In 1984, Vince Neil and Razzle, the drummer for Hanoi Rocks, left a party in Neil's powerful 1972 Ford Pantera to get more alcohol. While driving 65 mph in a 25 mph zone, Neil hit a wet patch, crossed into oncoming traffic, and crashed into two cars. Razzle died in the hospital, and Neil suffered cuts and cracked ribs. "While going 65 in a 25 miles per hour zone, the Pantera hit a wet patch of pavement, it crossed over into the opposite lane and crashed into two cars traveling the other way."

xref.title: Supergroup Lineup and Origins (1994-2001)
xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. And then in 2001, Alan Molder apparently helped record at least an album's worth of stuff."

xref.title: Assassination at El Rosa Villa Concert
xref.body: Dimebag Darrell, a revered guitarist from Pantera and Damageplan, was assassinated on December 8, 2004, exactly 24 years after John Lennon's death. During a Damageplan gig at the El Rosa Villa venue in Columbus, Ohio, attended by about 400 people, Nathan Gale rushed the stage and shot Darrell three times in the head at point-blank range as the band began their first song. "As the band started their first song at around 10-20 that night, a man named Nathan Gayle, 6'3", 250 pounds and wearing a Columbus Blue Jacket's hockey jersey, rushed the stage and shot Darryl with a 9mm semi-automatic pistol."

xref.title: Shooter's Background and Motivation
xref.body: Nathan Gale, the assailant, was a 6'3", 250-pound former Marine who had been discharged due to a diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia. Friends reported he had been "a little off" in the months leading up to the incident. While investigators explored theories—such as Gale being upset Darrell quit Pantera, or believing Darrell stole his lyrics or tried to steal his identity—the definitive motive for the assassination remains unknown. "Gayle was an expert who had told relatives he'd been discharged because of a diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia."
